translations.comment: Button an agent clicks to open a closed support ticket back up

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: The button reopens a ticket that was already closed, so 'Reabrir' (reopen) reflects the actual action more precisely and naturally than a plain 'Abrir'.

translations.disambiguationNote: This is a button an agent clicks to reopen a previously closed ticket, so it uses the action verb form 'Reabrir'. It differs from the other 'Open' in the batch, which is a status label describing that the support desk is currently open for business (an adjective/state, not a clickable action).

translations.comment: Label shown when the support desk is currently open for business

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Es un infinitivo, propio de un botón que ordena una acción; aquí se describe un estado, no se da una orden.
Se aleja del sentido literal de 'abierto' y podría confundirse con la disponibilidad de un agente en lugar del horario de atención.
La forma femenina no encaja; el sujeto implícito es el servicio de soporte y se usa la forma neutra/masculina habitual en estados de la interfaz.

translations.disambiguationNote: Aquí 'Open' describe el estado actual del servicio de soporte (está atendiendo), así que se usa el adjetivo 'Abierto'. Es distinto del botón 'ticket.button.open', que es una acción que ejecuta el agente para reabrir un ticket y debe ir en infinitivo ('Abrir').

translations.comment: Button an agent clicks to mark a ticket as resolved/closed

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: That's an adjective/past participle describing a state; this is an action button, which needs the infinitive in Spanish.

Though the comment mentions 'resolved', the English word is 'Close' and the paired button 'ticket.button.open' (Open a closed ticket) confirms the close/open pairing, so 'Cerrar' keeps the two consistent.

translations.disambiguationNote: This is a button an agent clicks to close a support ticket, so it uses the infinitive form 'Cerrar' as Spanish software conventions require for clickable actions. It pairs naturally with the 'Open' button ('Abrir') that reopens a closed ticket.

translations.comment: Button to publish a new post to the internal team feed

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: That is a noun ('a post'), which would be the wrong grammatical form for a clickable button; Spanish buttons use the infinitive.
Means 'send/submit' — too generic and closer to the mail sense; 'publish to a feed' is more precisely 'Publicar'.
That is the physical-mail sense used for mail.label.post; it does not apply to publishing to a team feed.

translations.disambiguationNote: Here 'Post' is the action of publishing a new message to the internal team feed, so it becomes the verb 'Publicar' on a button. This differs from mail.label.post, which is a noun about a physical mailing/correspondence address and would use a word like 'Correo' — never 'Publicar'.

translations.comment: Label for a physical mail correspondence address field

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Describes the postal service/mail itself rather than the address the field is meant to capture; less clear as an address-field label.
Too ambiguous in Spanish software—readers would assume email; loses the 'physical mail' sense entirely.
That is the 'publish to feed' meaning (feed.button.post), an action verb, not this address field.

translations.disambiguationNote: Here 'Post' is the British word for physical mail, and the developer note says this labels the field for a physical correspondence address, so it names an address, not an action. I chose 'Dirección postal' (mailing address). This is completely different from feed.button.post, which is a button to publish a post and would be translated as an action like 'Publicar'.
assumptions: The field captures the postal/mailing address, so a full 'Dirección postal' reads more naturally than a bare 'Correo postal'.

translations.comment: Button to assign a ticket to a specific agent

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: The button label should stay short; the surrounding context already makes clear it applies to a ticket, and other buttons in this batch are single-word infinitives.
That is an adjective/past participle describing a state, but this is a clickable action button, which requires the infinitive form.

translations.disambiguationNote: This is a button an agent clicks to assign a ticket to an agent, so I used the infinitive 'Asignar', which is the standard form for action buttons in Spanish software.

translations.comment: Field showing the due date/deadline for resolving a ticket

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Más largo; en una etiqueta de campo o columna suele bastar 'Vencimiento', que ya se entiende como fecha límite. Sería válido si se prefiere mayor claridad.
Correcto en significado, pero 'Vencimiento' es la convención más habitual en software para plazos y encaja mejor como nombre de campo.
Ese es el sentido de 'Due' en la factura (dinero pendiente), no el de este campo, que se refiere a una fecha límite.

translations.disambiguationNote: Aquí 'Due' se refiere a la fecha límite para resolver un ticket, por eso uso 'Vencimiento' (un plazo). En la factura, 'Due' (amount_due) significa dinero pendiente de pago, así que allí se traduce como 'Importe adeudado'; son sentidos distintos y no deben coincidir.
assumptions: Se prefiere una etiqueta corta; si el diseño da espacio, 'Fecha de vencimiento' sería igualmente apropiada.

translations.comment: Field showing the amount of money owed on an invoice

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Natural and common, but slightly less precise about the money being owed; 'adeudado' matches 'owed' more directly.
Valid, but frames it from the payer's action rather than stating what is owed on the invoice.
This means a due date/deadline, which is the correct sense for the ticket field, not for a money amount.
Works as an adjective but reads incomplete as a field label; adding 'Importe' makes it clearly a monetary amount.

translations.disambiguationNote: Here 'Due' refers to the sum of money owed on an invoice, so it's a noun phrase meaning the amount owed: 'Importe adeudado'. This is different from the ticket field, where 'Due' means a deadline/date and would be translated as 'Vencimiento'.

translations.comment: Button to share a ticket's link with another teammate

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Means 'send', which is a different action; the button is about sharing a link, not sending the ticket itself.
That is an adjective/past participle ('shared'), which describes a state, not a clickable action button.

translations.disambiguationNote: This is a button that lets someone share a ticket's link with a teammate, so I used the standard Spanish verb 'Compartir' in its infinitive form, which is the convention for buttons.

translations.comment: Button to export a report as a CSV or PDF file

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Es un sustantivo; en un botón la convención española es el infinitivo, no el nombre de la acción.
Es un participio/estado, no una orden; no corresponde a un botón de acción.

translations.disambiguationNote: Es el texto de un botón que exporta un informe a CSV o PDF. En español los botones usan el infinitivo, por eso 'Exportar'.
